c.tagline: A double-walled medieval fortress city, the largest of its kind still standing in Europe

card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small shops within La Cité

taxi.fare: Metered, roughly €3.50 flag fall plus per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard and reliable

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

walk: La Cité's cobbled streets are compact and walkable (though steep in places); the Ville Basse across the Aude River is a separate 15-20 min walk or short bus/taxi ride

safety.safety: Very safe city, popular with visitors of all ages
safety.crime: Petty theft in crowded La Cité during peak season is the main concern

hood_landmark.La Cité (Walled Citadel): The Château Comtal and Basilica within the double walls
hood_landmark.Pont Vieux Area: The medieval Pont Vieux bridge over the Aude River
hood_landmark.Canal du Midi (Bassin): The Canal du Midi's tree-lined port basin
hood_landmark.Trivalle: The Trivalle quarter beneath La Cité's walls

avoid.reason: Pickpockets work the packed lanes of the Cité in July-August, and the lower town around the train station can feel scruffy late at night.

hood_desc: The famous double-walled medieval fortress with 52 towers, restaurants, and shops; the essential base for first-time visitors, though very touristy by day.
The newer 19th-century town across the river, with everyday shops, markets, and more affordable dining away from the tourist crowds.
The historic bridge connecting La Cité and the Lower Town, with good photo views back up at the fortress walls.
A pleasant canal port with tree-shaded quays, popular for boat trips and cycling along the Canal du Midi.
A quiet residential quarter directly beneath La Cité's ramparts, offering a more local, budget-friendly base.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout France.

transit.pay: Cash or contactless card on board; rechargeable travel card available
transit.note: A shuttle bus connects La Cité to the Ville Basse and train station in peak season

transport.air: Carcassonne Airport (CCF) has budget flights from the UK and elsewhere in Europe; Toulouse-Blagnac (TLS) is a larger alternative about 1 hr away
transport.train: TGV and regional trains connect to Toulouse and onward to the rest of France
transport.bus: Regional buses connect to nearby Languedoc towns
transport.car: Well connected via the A61 motorway; parking is available near La Cité and in the Ville Basse

airport.name: Carcassonne Airport
airport.distance: ~5 km (10 min) from the city center

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: An Orange, SFR, or Bouygues tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for guides and tours
tip.r: Service is included by law; rounding up is a nice gesture, not expected
